title: Fix cumulative TMM heap segfault blocking Athenea endurance tests
body: When ~39 commented-out tests with implementations are uncommented and run, david_propup_engine.exe segfaults (exit 139) after propup_decision_engine_fusion. The crash is cumulative — running each half of the suite in isolation is stable (0 failures), running full suite together segfaults. Root cause: heap fragmentation or asymmetric allocate/deallocate in TieredMemoryManager across test lifecycles. make_test_runtime() helper (8 MiB pools) already exists and mitigates but does not fully fix. Proper fix requires auditing TieredMemoryManager::~TieredMemoryManager(), CoolPmrResource::do_deallocate, and RamFallbackPmrResource::do_deallocate for asymmetry, plus adding tmm.reset_for_testing() or process-level heap trim between run_one calls. This blocks ~27 Athenea/endurance/campaign tests from being enabled.

title: Fix MinGW CRT segfault in PropupReport::print() — replace std::ostream with hq_safe_write
body:
PropupReport::print() uses std::ostream operators (out << ...) inside the report printer. Under MinGW UCRT, when stdout is redirected to a pipe or file, std::ostream flush inside destructors causes a deterministic segfault (exit 139) during CRT TLS teardown. This blocks CI-style runs and any automated testing that captures output.

Currently only 2 uses of hq_safe_write() across the entire code/src and code/include directories (grep found 2). hq_safe_write is the canonical shim that bypasses the MinGW CRT piping crash.

Task:
1. Replace ALL std::ostream output in PropupReport::print() and run_all_propups exception handler with hq_safe_write(std::format(...)).
2. Verify redirection stability: for i in {1..50}; do ./david_propup_engine.exe > out.txt 2>&1 || echo "FAIL run $i"; done — must return 0 every time.
3. While in the file, also audit any remaining std::cout/std::cerr usage in david_propup_engine.cpp (53 ostream uses detected) and convert diagnostic paths to hq_safe_write.

This is a crash-hazard fix, not a feature.
